1) Roles / DPA exhibits: we’ll accept controller/processor split as proposed in your Exhibit A with one adjustment: we need a narrow processor subprocessor clause that permits Redwood to engage managed hosting providers but requires customer notice for non-standard cross-border subprocessors. See proposed clause in attached DPA_Roles_Matrix.xlsx.

2) SCCs acceptance & transfer impact: Redwood can sign the EU Commission SCCs. To address the APAC subprocessors ask: we will add a fallback Private deployment commitment in Appendix A to restrict hosting territories if a legal/regulatory block is identified, subject to a reasonable migration timeline and associated costs. Proposed language in the Drive doc (link below).

3) Data deletion & retention: standard post-termination deletion is 60 days, with a 12-month certified backup retention for specific regulated customers if requested and paid as an add-on. We can move to a defined deletion window in the DPA; I propose wording: “Primary data deleted within 60 days; no residual production copies retained; customer-specific certified backups retained up to 12 months if elected.”

4) Evidence / audit checklist: I created a short checklist (see DPA_Roles_Matrix.xlsx) that maps processor tasks to standard artifacts (SCCs, SOC2 report, KMS key inventory, subprocessor roster). We can provide the evidence package under NDA or via our shared drive link.
